_doc: The exact schema of data.sqlite per package type (format 1, except where a case states its own formatVersion: sentences is format 2): the common statements first, then the type's tables and indexes in this order (sqlite_master of a built package holds exactly these, plus SQLite's own autoindexes). order is the row order of each table in the content hash (README.md, Versioning); it is the primary key where the table has one. qq_package holds packageKeys (grammar also levels_json); every value is TEXT (numbers in decimal, languages as a JSON array). JSON lists and objects are TEXT columns holding JSON, as on the server. Decoded by server/internal/datapkg (A5).
common: CREATE TABLE qq_package (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE qq_sources (type TEXT NOT NULL, pack_id TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, version TEXT NOT NULL, license TEXT NOT NULL, attribution TEXT NOT NULL, notice TEXT NOT NULL, license_files TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (type, pack_id))

tables.name: entries
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE entries (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, language TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, ext_key TEXT NOT NULL, pri INTEGER NOT NULL, uk INTEGER NOT NULL, attrs TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.name: forms
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE forms (entry_id INTEGER NOT NULL, ord INTEGER NOT NULL, text TEXT NOT NULL, flags TEXT NOT NULL, pri INTEGER NOT NULL)

tables.name: readings
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE readings (entry_id INTEGER NOT NULL, ord INTEGER NOT NULL, type TEXT NOT NULL, value TEXT NOT NULL, plain TEXT NOT NULL, flags TEXT NOT NULL, pri INTEGER NOT NULL)

tables.name: senses
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE senses (entry_id INTEGER NOT NULL, dictionary_id INTEGER NOT NULL, ord INTEGER NOT NULL, pos TEXT NOT NULL, tags TEXT NOT NULL, glosses TEXT NOT NULL, xrefs TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.name: links
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE links (from_id INTEGER NOT NULL, to_id INTEGER NOT NULL, type TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (from_id, to_id, type))

tables.name: dictionaries
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE dictionaries (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pack_id TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, version TEXT NOT NULL, language TEXT NOT NULL, license TEXT NOT NULL, attribution TEXT NOT NULL, notice TEXT NOT NULL)

indexes: CREATE INDEX forms_entry ON forms (entry_id, ord)
CREATE INDEX readings_entry ON readings (entry_id, ord)
CREATE INDEX senses_entry ON senses (entry_id, dictionary_id, ord)
CREATE INDEX links_to ON links (to_id, type)

tables.name: schemes
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE schemes (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, pack_id TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL, unit TEXT NOT NULL, language TEXT NOT NULL, version TEXT NOT NULL, license TEXT NOT NULL, attribution TEXT NOT NULL, notice TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.name: levels
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE levels (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, scheme_id INTEGER NOT NULL, ord INTEGER NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.name: level_members
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE level_members (level_id INTEGER NOT NULL, entry_id INTEGER NOT NULL, derived INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (level_id, entry_id))

cases._doc: pinyin may be "": a pack sentence without a reading (the pack left it out rather than guess one, e.g. a word with several readings); a client shows no reading line for it. Format 2: every sentence carries its credit, credit_id (the sentence's id at its source, Tatoeba; 0 for none) and credit_owner (its owner as the source lists it, may be ""), credit_tr_id and credit_tr_owner (the same for the translation shown with it); the link of a credit is the source's page of the id, https://tatoeba.org/en/sentences/show/<id>, not stored. Format 1 (no credit columns) is not read.

tables.name: sentences
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE sentences (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, entry_id INTEGER NOT NULL, hanzi TEXT NOT NULL, pinyin TEXT NOT NULL, translation TEXT NOT NULL, credit_id INTEGER NOT NULL, credit_owner TEXT NOT NULL, credit_tr_id INTEGER NOT NULL, credit_tr_owner TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.name: frequency
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE frequency (term TEXT NOT NULL, reading TEXT NOT NULL, rank INTEGER NOT NULL, display TEXT NOT NULL)

indexes: CREATE INDEX frequency_term ON frequency (term, reading)

tables.name: components
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE components (char TEXT PRIMARY KEY, parts TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.name: component_parts
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE component_parts (part TEXT PRIMARY KEY, strokes INTEGER NOT NULL)

tables.name: clips
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE clips (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT NOT NULL, form TEXT NOT NULL, reading_key TEXT NOT NULL, sha256 TEXT NOT NULL, ext TEXT NOT NULL, bytes INTEGER NOT NULL, license TEXT NOT NULL, attribution TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL)

indexes: CREATE INDEX clips_lookup ON clips (kind, form, reading_key)

tables.name: lessons
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE lessons (lesson_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, level_id TEXT NOT NULL, ord INTEGER NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, summary TEXT NOT NULL, content TEXT NOT NULL)

indexes: CREATE INDEX lessons_level ON lessons (level_id, ord)

tables.name: strokes
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE strokes (char TEXT PRIMARY KEY, data TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.name: lemma_rules
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE lemma_rules (language TEXT PRIMARY KEY, rules_json TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.name: pictures
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE pictures (concept TEXT PRIMARY KEY, label TEXT NOT NULL, credit TEXT NOT NULL, svg TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.name: map
tables.sql: CREATE TABLE map (language TEXT NOT NULL, target TEXT NOT NULL, sense INTEGER NOT NULL, concept TEXT NOT NULL, score INTEGER NOT NULL, basis TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (language, target, sense, concept))
